title: Eat from the harvest, give its due, and do not waste.
subtitle: Gardens, palms and olives, with three instructions

row.title: His, with a share for others

then: The idolaters had carved up crops and cattle with invented rules. Allah reminds them {idea}He produced the gardens, trellised and wild.{/idea} Mujahid said when the poor are present on harvest day, {reward}give them some of it.{/reward} Ibn Kathir reads the warning on excess as mainly about eating, citing: eat and drink without extravagance or arrogance.
now: Payday lands. The first thought is the new phone, the takeaway, the upgrade. {reward}This verse puts someone else's share right next to yours{/reward}, on the same day the money arrives. {trap}And it warns against eating and spending past what you need.{/trap}
old: What I earned is mine to enjoy however I like.
new: It came from Allah. I enjoy it, share some, and do not overdo it.
try: On your next payday, give a small amount to someone in need the same day.

title: Animals to carry and feed you. Eat, and skip Satan's footsteps.
subtitle: Provision received with gratitude, not invented rules
then: Ibn Zayd explained it: some animals carry people and loads, others are {reward}eaten and milked, with their wool used for mats and clothes.{/reward} All are Allah's provision. The pagans had followed devilish ideas in forbidding some of them. {trap}Do not follow Satan's footsteps; he is a clear enemy.{/trap}
now: Your wool jumper, your morning milk, the leather of your shoes. {reward}All of it came from animals Allah made useful to you.{/reward} {trap}Satan rarely asks for a leap. He asks for one small step at a time.{/trap}
old: Satan only matters when I am tempted by something huge.
new: Satan works in footsteps. I watch the small steps, and I thank Allah for what He gave.
try: Look at one thing you use today that came from an animal, and thank Allah for it by name.

title: Male or female, or what is in the womb? Show your proof.
subtitle: Sheep and goats, and a question about invented bans
then: Ibn Kathir says these verses expose the ignorance of the Arabs before Islam, who banned certain animals. Ibn Abbas explained: {idea}Allah did not forbid any of these.{/idea} Does a womb give anything but males and females? So why ban some and allow others? {trap}Tell me with knowledge, if you are truthful.{/trap}
now: Someone tells you a thing is forbidden. You ask where it says so, and they get offended. {idea}Asking for knowledge is not rudeness. The Quran itself asks it.{/idea} Ask politely, and keep asking.
old: Questioning a religious claim is disrespectful.
new: The Quran itself asks for proof. I can ask, kindly, where a rule comes from.
try: Next time you hear a surprising religious claim, ask gently: what is the source?

title: Were you there when Allah gave this command?
subtitle: Camels and cattle, and lies told to mislead
then: The same question repeats for camels and cattle. Then a sharper one: {idea}were you present when Allah ordered this?{/idea} Ibn Kathir says it mocks their invented bans. {trap}No one is more unjust than one who lies about Allah to mislead people without knowledge.{/trap} He names Amr bin Luhay as the first to change the religion this way.
now: You forward a message: "The Prophet ﷺ said..." You never checked it. Hundreds of people now believe it. {trap}One unchecked claim can mislead many.{/trap} {idea}Were you there? Do you know?{/idea}
old: Sharing a religious message is always good, even if I am not sure it is true.
new: Spreading claims about Allah without knowledge can mislead people. I check first.
try: Before forwarding any religious message today, check its source or do not send it.

title: The list of forbidden food is short, and mercy covers need.
subtitle: What revelation actually names, against invented bans
then: The Prophet ﷺ is told to answer those who invented bans: {idea}I do not find in what was revealed to me{/idea} anything forbidden except these. Ibn Kathir notes other texts add to this list. Ibn Abbas said: {reward}what Allah allowed is lawful, what He forbade is unlawful, and there is no sin in what He did not mention.{/reward}
now: Some people make religion feel like a minefield, where every step might be wrong. {idea}Allah's limits are clear and few compared to the open land.{/idea} {reward}And when you are truly forced, His mercy is there.{/reward}
old: Religion is mostly a long list of things I cannot do.
new: Allah's limits are clear and few, and His mercy is wide.
try: Make a note of five good things Allah has made fully allowed for you, and enjoy one today with thanks.

title: Some restrictions came as the price of rebellion.
subtitle: Extra limits earned by defiance, and the loophole trick
then: Allah tells of foods He forbade to the Children of Israel, and says {trap}this was a recompense for their rebellion{/trap}, not a rule they took from Ya'qub as they claimed. Ibn Kathir cites the hadith warning against those who, when fats were forbidden, {trap}melted them down, sold them, and used the price.{/trap}
now: You would never take a bribe. But a "gift" after the contract? You would never cheat a customer. But the small print? {trap}Renaming a thing to slip past a limit is the oldest trick.{/trap} {idea}Respect what the rule is for.{/idea}
old: If I find a technical way around a rule, I am not doing anything wrong.
new: Getting around Allah's limits with tricks is its own kind of rebellion.
try: Think of one place you use a technicality to get around something. Drop the trick this week.

title: If they deny you, say: your Lord's mercy is vast.
subtitle: Hope and warning in the same breath
then: Even when the Prophet ﷺ is rejected, his reply opens with {reward}your Lord is the Owner of vast mercy{/reward}, an invitation. Then the warning that His punishment is not turned away from criminals. Ibn Kathir notes that {idea}Allah often joins hope and warning{/idea}, as at the end of this same surah.
now: You have messed up badly, again. Part of you says it is over. {reward}The first thing this verse says, even to those rejecting the Prophet ﷺ, is that mercy is vast.{/reward} {idea}The warning is real. So is the open door.{/idea}
old: After what I have done, there is only punishment waiting for me.
new: His mercy is vast and open to me. The warning is there so I walk through that door.
try: Make istighfar today for the one thing you think is too big to be forgiven.

title: If Allah wanted, we would not have done it, they said.
subtitle: Blaming fate for your own choices

row.title: it happened, so it is fine

then: The idolaters argued: {trap}if Allah had willed, we and our fathers would not have done shirk{/trap}, so He must approve. Ibn Kathir says earlier nations used the same excuse. If it were true, He would not have punished them. {idea}Do you have any knowledge? You only follow guesses.{/idea}
now: "It was written for me." You say it about the lie, the shortcut, the habit you keep feeding. {trap}Decree becomes a blanket you hide under.{/trap} {idea}Allah's knowledge of your choice does not make the choice His.{/idea}
old: If I did it, Allah must have wanted it, so I am off the hook.
new: Allah knowing what I will do does not make wrong right. I still own my choices.
try: Catch one moment today where you blame fate. Replace it with: I chose this, and I can choose again.

title: The final argument belongs to Allah.
subtitle: He could have guided all of you
then: After their excuse about fate, the reply: {idea}with Allah is the perfect, far-reaching argument.{/idea} Ibn Kathir says He has the perfect wisdom to guide or misguide whom He wills, and is pleased with the believers. Ad-Dahhak said: {trap}no one has an excuse if he disobeys Allah.{/trap}
now: You have rehearsed your excuse for years. Busy, stressed, raised that way, nobody taught me. {idea}Picture saying it to the One who knows every hour you had.{/idea} Better to drop the excuse now and just ask for help.
old: I have good reasons for not changing, and Allah will accept them.
new: Allah's proof is complete. Instead of excuses, I can ask Him for guidance.
try: Write your favorite excuse down, then cross it out and write a dua for help instead.

title: Bring your witnesses. If they lie, do not testify with them.
subtitle: Refusing to join a false testimony
then: The Prophet ﷺ is told to ask them to {idea}bring witnesses that Allah forbade this.{/idea} If they testify anyway, Ibn Kathir says {trap}their testimony is false{/trap}, so do not testify with them, and do not follow the desires of those who deny the signs and set up equals to their Lord.
now: The whole family agrees a relative is to blame. Everyone in the meeting nods along to a claim you know is wrong. {trap}It is easy to add your nod.{/trap} {idea}You can stay silent, or say what you know, but do not sign off on a lie.{/idea}
old: If everyone else is saying it, it is fine for me to agree.
new: When a group backs something false, I do not add my voice to it.
try: In the next group conversation where something unfair is said, decline to agree, even quietly.

title: Come, hear what your Lord truly forbade.
subtitle: The first of the commands Ibn Mas'ud called a sealed will
then: After all the invented food bans, the Prophet ﷺ says: {idea}come, I will recite what your Lord actually forbade.{/idea} Ibn Mas'ud said whoever wants to read the will of the Messenger ﷺ on which he placed his seal should read these verses. Ibn Kathir notes {reward}kindness to parents{/reward} sits right next to worshipping Allah alone.
now: You argue about small details of religion online while not calling your mother back for a week. {idea}These verses are the real list.{/idea} {reward}Your parents are near the top, right after Allah.{/reward}
old: Being religious is mostly about the small details I argue about.
new: Allah's real list starts with Him alone, kindness to parents, and protecting life.
try: Call or visit one of your parents today, or make dua for them if they have passed.

title: Fair measure, honest words, even against your own family.
subtitle: Orphans, weights, testimony and promises
then: Ibn Abbas said that when this was revealed, guardians of orphans became so careful they kept the orphans' food separate. Allah then eased it. Ibn Kathir says {idea}justice is commanded in actions and words, with near and far relatives alike.{/idea} And {reward}no one is burdened beyond what they can bear{/reward}; an honest mistake after real effort is not a sin.
now: Your brother is in the wrong in the family dispute, and everyone looks at you. {idea}Being fair now costs something.{/idea} The same with the bill you split, the hours you log, the promise you made. {reward}Allah asks only what you can carry.{/reward}
old: I am fair, except when it is my own family.
new: Justice counts most when it is against my own people. And Allah asks only what I can bear.
try: In one small matter today, choose the fair option even if it costs you or someone close.

title: One straight path, and many side roads that scatter you.
subtitle: The line drawn in the sand
then: Ibn Mas'ud reported the Prophet ﷺ {idea}drew a straight line in the sand and said: this is Allah's path.{/idea} Then he drew lines to its right and left: {trap}on each of these paths is a devil calling to it.{/trap} Then he recited this verse. Ibn Kathir notes the path is singular because truth is one, and the other ways are many.
now: A new guru every month. A new trend every week. Each one shouts from its own side road. {trap}You end up scattered, pulled in every direction.{/trap} {idea}Hold the one line, and the noise from the sides gets easier to ignore.{/idea}
old: Trying every path is how I will find the right one.
new: There is one straight path, and the side roads exist to pull me off it.
try: Draw a straight line on paper with lines branching off. Name one side road you want to stop walking.
